definitions.explanation: To cut a shape or design into a hard material like wood or stone.
To cut letters or designs into a surface.
To create permanent designs on skin.

examples.english: I carve a Buddha statue from wood.
I engrave a name in stone.
I get a tattoo on my arm.

examples.japanese: {趣味|しゅみ}で{木彫|きぼ}りの{人形|にんぎょう}を{彫|ほ}っている。
examples.english: I carve wooden figurines as a hobby.

examples.japanese: {職人|しょくにん}が{細|こま}かい{模様|もよう}を{丁寧|ていねい}に{彫|ほ}っていた。
examples.english: The craftsman was carefully carving a detailed pattern.

examples.japanese: {記念|きねん}にペンダントに{日付|ひづけ}を{彫|ほ}ってもらった。
examples.english: I had the date engraved on a pendant as a memento.

examples.japanese: {墓石|ぼせき}に{故人|こじん}の{名前|なまえ}と{生年月日|せいねんがっぴ}を{彫|ほ}る。
examples.english: The deceased's name and date of birth are engraved on the gravestone.

examples.japanese: {背中|せなか}に{龍|りゅう}の{刺青|いれずみ}を{彫|ほ}った。
examples.english: I had a dragon tattoo done on my back.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}では{刺青|いれずみ}を{彫|ほ}ると{温泉|おんせん}に{入|はい}れないことがある。
examples.english: In Japan, having a tattoo can prevent you from entering hot springs.

notes:
{彫|ほ}る means to carve or engrave into a hard surface.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)
- Takes を particle: {像|ぞう}を{彫|ほ}る

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {彫刻|ちょうこく}: sculpture, carving
- {木彫|きぼ}り: woodcarving
- {彫|ほ}り{物|もの}: carving, engraving
- {彫|ほ}りが{深|ふか}い: having well-defined features (of a face)

HOMOPHONE:
- {掘|ほ}る (to dig) has the same reading but different meaning and kanji.
- {彫|ほ}る: to carve INTO a surface
- {掘|ほ}る: to dig OUT from the ground
